analysis.name: Alfred Mele
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Mele is one of the most informed professors at FSU in his subject matter and wants to see you succeed. Very heavy in readings, and his TA does most of the grading, which can seem harsh at times but is aimed at comprehension of the subject.

Mele gives strikingly clear hypothetical examples that are typically designed to pump your intuitions about particular cases and arose skepticism of virtually any general principles. He leaves you in a state of aporia without providing much in the way of positive answers. This method of philosophical inquiry is strikingly characteristic of the 80s.

An author of several immemorable works, Dr. Mele will impress into intelligent minds problems that challege modern philosophers.  However, concerning his position on freedom and free will, Mele is a intellectual hitman, unable to reveal his position on such matters as libertarianism and incompatibilism.

review_highlights.comment: Absolute GOAT of a teacher. Man he is one of the most caring and passionate professors I ever had. The best teacher at FSU and gives advice to any situation you need. If you made it through 3403 and had no idea what was going on, this class and Dr. S make all the concepts and math make sense. Fantastic professor who tells you everything you need for the exams and is overall just a great guy. Do the exam practice problems. Three exams (final cumulative), two easy projects, and one presentation make up your grade.

I feel Dr. S is a one-of-a-kind teacher, who fully embraces his position. It's rare you find someone so passionate in teaching that it seeps through every aspect of class. Very well thought out structure and material. Gives advice on what to do on the exam, as well as great real-world advice. If you seem him available, click "register" ASAP!

Dr. S is the best professor I have ever had. As an MSF student, I've taken 4 classes with him, and he consistently makes challenging concepts easy to understand. He has an open-door policy and is always available to help with class material, career advice, or the MSF program. Any student would be  extremely lucky to have him. He rocks.

So much extra credit AND he provided a free opportunity for us to get our Excel certification (passing the certification exam also counted for extra credit, plus those exams are usually expensive to take). Only a handful of his assignments got tricky but he provides so many resources.

Best Professor EVER. If you watch his video lectures and just do the assignments, you are set. This has been my favorite class at FSU so far and I genuinely have so much fun doing his assignments. analysis.name: Ashwanth Francis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Francis is a great professor. The class isn't truly hard at all, you just need to manage your time (including other classes) well enough to commit the material to memory. That's really all it is. He certainly likes to put you on the spot in lectures. Some people hate that, but personally I see it as a method of positive reinforcement.

Dr. Francis is an amazing person. He is so kind and truely cares for his students. The exams were very straight forward. You just need to read the textbook and go over his slides to do well. I was expecting to get a B+, but with the extra credit and exam retakes, it brought my grade up to an A. Very accessible in and out of class but not via email

Tests are very easy due to their format, and his lectures are concise and include only the information you need to know without a lot of extra content. Attendance is not mandatory and you can easily pass without attending as long as you study a day or two before exams. Lectures are interesting and he is funny and respectful. Highly recommend.
Dr. Francis's grading was extremely fair: 5% extra credit if you went to class every day. He goes on tangents sometimes while lecturing so it can be hard to follow along.
Best professor I have ever had. Take him if you truly want to learn and have fun while doing so.

analysis.name: Amid Ardakani
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor seemed scary at first but after the first week or so you realize that he's actually really cool. He really cares about teaching which is something that you don't see often. He gives out study guides for tests and overall has really good insights on things. One of the best classes I took in my major.

Amid hosts an awesome class in Economics of Development. His lectures are always fun and interesting. He helps students prepare for the tests through detailed and relevant practice tests. He offers PLENTY of extra credit. He counts attendance, though, which is 10% of the grade.

TBH, when I saw all his amazing ratings, I thought he'd be a little more laid back. However, as the class went on he did become more chill lol. But the class overall wasn't that bad, lots of assignments to help your grade, he gave study guides that pretty much showed what were on the test. It was annoying that you needed a 95%+ to get an A tho

He likes to add humor to the lectures, so it's sometimes interesting. Only 30 percent of the class is based on exams, so you'll get a decent grade. When I took him more than half of the assignments counted towards the grade, but it was all just book reports for each chapter. There is a paper at the end, but it's easy to get through.

Dr. Ardakani truly cares about his students. His classes are a lot of work, but are graded leniently to give everyone an advantage. He learns everyones names and is very understanding. You can tell he wants his students to succeed and enjoys teaching. I decided to take another course with him (Eco of Middle East) after taking Eco of Development.

analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took Dr. Wang's class Fall 2020, during the pandemic where classes were online. He was extremely accommodating and allowed our tests to be open note. The projects were challenging but not unreasonably so, especially if you seek out help from the TAs. He is fair and his tests are very similar to quizzes. Definitely one of the good ones in CS dept!

Andy is probably one of the best professors in CS at FSU. He goes in-depth during his lectures and takes the time to answer any questions students have. He conveys the material in an easy to understand way. He was always available outside of class as well. Prepare yourself, the projects are very hard, but it's expected since it's a capstone class.

Intro to OS is definitely a hard class, but Dr. Wang is the best professor to take it with. His exams can be a little difficult, but the material covered on them is clearly defined. The hardest part is the programming assignments. They take a lot of time and effort, but if you go to recitation, ask questions, and start early, you'll do just fine.

Dr. Wang has a true passion for what he teaches. The class can be challenging, but he teaches you the material in such a way that the difficult programs go from being impossible to understandable. If you put in the time to learn he will make you significantly better at programming. He's amazing. There arent a lot of great professors like him.

I took Dr. Wang's class online in Fall'20. Tests were open note along with quizzes. He really cares about his students & goes the extra mile to make sure everyone understands. There are 3-4 group projects that are tough, but if you stay on top of it you will do just fine. The TA's are helpful and the projects are beneficial to learning.

analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 111 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: What I thought would be the easiest class turned out to be my hardest. Studied forever and still BOMBED the first exam. Lectures are unclear, PowerPoints are confusing, and there's no direction on what to study. Every assignment is through McGraw-Hill, which makes learning MISERABLE. She expects us to "grasp" every possible concept in the textbook.

Everyone failed the first exam and she only gave a hilarious 5-point curve. She did offer help but no extra credit. Communication is subpar and the class is overly complicated for no reason. Not allowing a graphing calculator makes it worse considering how hard the formulas are. She's very nice, but the way this course is structured is laughable.

4.0 FSU student; 95% in FIN3403 (Gary Bliss). Class isn't hard conceptually—it's the sheer volume and little exam guidance, especially online. First exam wrecked grades; afterward they added a review and formula sheet. In-person is a cakewalk; online feels like “read the whole textbook and get tested.” Notes are wordy and confusing.

The lectures are not good. Going into the class it seems like you are missing something that she should've taught. So many people failed the first exam this semester she let people retake it but there were no available test sessions, and called her students failures for failing it. I now have to drop this course which may offset my entire plan.

I guess this is what you get when you pick the only teacher available for the one class you need. I'll probably end up failing, considering how poorly I'm doing right now with the lovely zero extra credit opportunities. I think she forgot this isn't the only class we're taking at FSU. My mental health and GPA is declining as I write this review. :(

Attendance is a must, but if you put in the effort, you'll get a whole lot out of the experience!
